stuck_detail: Learner assigns two opposed quantities to a single owner and reasons as if one entity receives both.

core.intent: Surface that the learner is assigning both opposed quantities to one owner, by forcing explicit naming of the distinct owner each quantity acts upon — making the two-owner structure visible before any further reasoning.
core.trigger: Learner claims the two opposed quantities 'act on the same thing' or implicitly treats them as competing claims on a single owner.
core.shape: Ask, for each opposed quantity in turn: 'This quantity — which specific owner does it act upon? Name the owner.' Then ask: 'Are those two owners the same entity or different entities?' The contradiction surfaces in the learner's own answers.
guards: Do not accept a process or interaction as the named owner — require a discrete, identifiable entity.
Do not move on until both owners are named explicitly and separately; vague answers like 'between them' restart the question.
Do not supply the owner names yourself; the diagnostic value comes from the learner producing them.
If the learner names the same owner twice, hold that answer up and re-ask: 'Same entity both times — is that right?'

rendered_examples.subject: kite flying
rendered_examples.example: OK, we have two forces — one at a time. The string pulls the kite upward: which object does that force act on? Name it. Now the kite pulls the string downward: which object does that force act on? Name it. Are those two objects the same thing or different things?

rendered_examples.subject: layang-layang
rendered_examples.example: Oke, iki ana rong gaya — siji-siji. Senar narik layang-layang munggah: gaya iki tumiba ing obyek endi? Jenengna. Saiki layang-layang narik senar mudhun: gaya iki tumiba ing obyek endi? Jenengna. Obyek loro iku padha apa beda?
rendered_examples.back_translation: OK, two forces, one at a time. The string pulls the kite up: which object does this act on? Name it. Now the kite pulls the string down: which object does this act on? Name it. Same object or different?

stuck_detail: Learner accepts the two owners differ yet still concludes the opposed quantities cancel to zero net effect on each.

core.intent: Reframe so each opposed quantity is recorded only in the account of the owner it acts upon; establish that two quantities can sum or cancel only within the same account; conclude that quantities in two different owners' accounts never meet and cannot cancel; redirect the learner to read each owner's outcome from that owner's account alone.
core.trigger: Learner accepts that the two owners are different yet still concludes the opposed quantities cancel, yielding zero net effect on each owner.
core.shape: Introduce a 'separate account per owner' register. Place each quantity only in the account of its owner. Ask: 'To decide what happens to owner A, which account do we read?' Then: 'Does owner B's quantity appear anywhere in owner A's account?' The emptiness of the cross-entry refutes cancellation without argument.
guards: Keep the account one-directional: a quantity flows into the account of the entity it acts upon, never the entity it originates from.
Do not allow a shared or combined account; if the learner proposes one, ask which single owner it belongs to.
Insist cancellation requires two entries in the same account; if 'cancel' is used across accounts, pause and have them locate both entries in one account first.
Close one owner's account before opening the other; do not let quantities slide across accounts mid-reading.
Resolve each owner's motion separately; do not conflate the two outcomes into one combined statement.

rendered_examples.subject: layang-layang
rendered_examples.example: Ayo bukak rekening loro — siji kanggo layang-layang, siji kanggo senar. Saben gaya mung dicathet ing rekening sing nampa. Senar narik layang-layang -> rekening layang-layang. Layang-layang narik senar -> rekening senar. Kanggo ngerti layang-layang obah apa ora, aku maca rekening layang-layang wae. Gaya saka layang-layang ora ana ing rekening layang-layang, to? Dadi ora ana sing mbatalake tarikan senar.
rendered_examples.back_translation: Open two accounts — one for the kite, one for the string. Each force is recorded only in the account of the receiver. String->kite goes in the kite's account; kite->string in the string's. To know if the kite moves, read only the kite's account; the kite's own force isn't there, so nothing cancels the string's pull.

rendered_examples.subject: kite flying
rendered_examples.example: Open two separate accounts — one for the kite, one for the string. Every force goes only into the account of what it acts on. String-pulls-kite goes into the kite's account; kite-pulls-string into the string's. To work out what the kite does, read only the kite's account. Show me the string's own force in the kite's account — it's not there, so nothing cancels the string's pull.
